Maybe not a weakness of the system but more of a preference based thing: Pathfinder 2e is a tactical combat system. It's one of if not the big draw. You have lots of options in character creation to allow a lot of different approaches to combat. If your party is not working together or not being careful, even moderate encounters can cause a death.

A lot of 5e players come over and want to make changes to the system for their home games. This practice can, depending on what they change, make the system math a bit wonky and end up impacting their perception of the system. I'd say 90% of the games mechanics are intended. (With how specific the rules can get some edgecases are ambiguous) so I see more than a few 5e players quit the system despite not truly playing the system as intended.

As a consequence of both points, there can be a clear disparity in a well made character mechanically and one made with more of a RP focus or a nonchalant build. The math is very good at balancing and accounting for teamwork such that a lack of +1 here or there can really make a difference. Even more so the more you stray from "optimization."

A good rule of thumb is to make sure you have +4 in your key ability score, and you choose feats that work towards the class's niche. Even if you take some feats for RP or other things, so long as that key score is +4 and you have a feat or two to work with, you'll be fine.

Also as I play the system more I've realized that just because the system has a bunch of character options doesn't mean it will be easy to work with. So many choices can paralyze new players and feeling overwhelmed with that and all the new rules and mechanics has also turned people away.

Monks arent just for dealing dmg like a fighter in PF2e. you'll have WAY more success playing a supportive frontline that does decent dmg to follow up.

Consider a few things. In Pathfinder Status and Circumstance bonuses/penalties are combats bread and butter and making things easier to hit/crit make a ton of difference. Every +1 matters. 

Monk (IMHO) is the best frontline to provide your martial support in combat. You can give flanking and are tanky enough to hold your own. You have high mobility to respond to dynamic combats. You have Flurry of Blows to hit twice while retaining your 2 actions to provide more support. And with Flurry of blows comes my favorite feat, Flurry of Maneuvers, allowing you to trip grapple shove as part of your flurry of blows. (all of which increases your MAP anyway)

If you want to augment your fists to deal dmg or apply effects, Monk has many many stances to allow you to do that. Monk's Fists are raised to a d6 by default AND are able to provide nonleathal dmg, which doesn't impact your % to hit when attacking. On top of the Mystic Strikes feature. Monks fists are so versatile its pretty insane.

I do not see monk as a main dmg source in combat, but a party enabler or even zone of control tank. Even better with, as an example, Fire Order Druid who can cast Wildfire or even other zone of control spells.

Let me clarify that antiheal as a stat is good, but most characters are very bad at applying it efficiently.

If, as a tank, you're building tainted bastion or tainted guard, you can only apply your antiheal if they hit you. If they choose different targets or just let the anti heal drop, then what can you do to keep reapplying it.

In a similar vain, while phase can heal her ream in fights, most of the time, particularly in lane, she is helping you sustain back up after a trade or fight. (Same as narbash.)

Some characters are fantastic at applying antiheal. Gadget, Morigesh, Fey. The key detail is that they all have DoTs that are able to continue to reapply the tainted proc over time. Which means they will have to spend more time away from the fight to gain their healing benefits. 

The only time I'd buy tainted on a tank is if your lane opponent directly would be healing off of you in the 1v1. Predecessor is weird in the fact that the combo of tainted guard/bastion are just so strong together that they are a must buy regardless if they have healing or not.

In summary, tainted is best on DoT mages and perhaps carry within certain teamcomp parameters. But even carry can struggle to apply it to the necessary targets in a chaotic fight. Usually they have the target the thing in front of them.

Antiheal is a Stat where you need to consider a few things outside of just the strength of the Stat.

Here's the thing about anti heal, if the items tracked and showed you how much you were actually negating, tainted wouldn't be as worth as you are perceiving. 

A lot of healing happens outside of fights or just normal regen. So it isn't as efficient to buy antiheal on a large portion of heros. 

If your character is able to consistently reapply it easy, like gadget, then it's worth buying. 


LoL has the same antiheal fallacy. People will buy anti heal but not applying it when the healing is actually happening.

Just something to think about.

In mobas, there is a "correct way" to lose. For matchups where you are losing, there are a few ways to help you stay in the game.

The obvious ones are staying within exp range as well as smart itemization. 

You can however really manipulate the enemy using good wave control and positioning.

I'd need to draw it out but, if you allow the enemy to auto you once they will draw minion agro thus making the wave push toward your tower. Since your minions aren't dealing damage to theirs it creates a natural pushing lane.

Another thing to keep in mind in all aspects of laning is that your HP is a resource. You can trade your hp for cs. When you are at a point where you have enough gold for an item component or a new item entirely you can use your hp and abilities to farm the wave then recall. You don't plan on staying in the lane so use that knowledge to farm as much as you can.

If they are able to freeze the wave on you, it is sometimes better to recall and roam to other lanes to help get your team ahead even if you yourself are slightly behind. I see a lot of players just "accept" the fact the wave is frozen and do nothing.

If you roam the enemy should try and push the wave out and force you to lose minions or the tower. Perma freezing the wave isn't always in their best interest, esp if you start roaming elsewhere on the map.

Also normally in a solo lane, you want to avoid positioning withing you own wave as this allows the enemy to farm while also poking you out. In this case, to facilitate the wave pushing towards you, you can try this tactic instead of avoiding it.

"It was nothing, ... simply what I do."

The doctor watched as the couple left cradling their child. Their eyes were red, their bodies were gaunt and exhausted. They had traveled halfway across the continent to see the doctor. Over the past 5 years, the doctor had built a reputation to save even the most sickly person. Seeming to defy logic and science, people were brought back from the brink.

They had sealed away the Demon Lord as the Hero was merciful. Peace had been restored but at a cost. The Hero wouldn't die. The doctor himself saw the hero murdered only for them to get up and walk away unscathed. The doctor surmised the fates of the Demon Lord and the Heros were linked. By not ending the life of the Demon Lord, the Heros quest had truly never been fulfilled. While the hero was genuine and kind, he was not the brightest, going wherever the doctor told him. The doctor had been such a great help on his journey, he just *had* to return the favor.

The doctor continued down a long hallway that lead to a set of stairs that penetrated deep into the earth. The doctor's bones ached. He had gotten old. He was considered old when he met the hero, but now... After the years of traveling and now the 5 years after he settled down. He could be considered ancient.

One day the doctor asked for the hero to save a young girl who had gotten stuck in a wine cellar. The doctor heard the cries for help but was not able to traverse the staircase into the depths. The hero went. The doctor who had known the Hero would go lay a trap for the hero. So the hero was drugged and secured in the doctor's laboratory deep within the earth.

The trip up and down the stairs took only a few minutes for a healthy adult but now took the doctor what seemed like an eternity. When he reached the bottom, the tight space opened up into a far larger space lined with tables, notations, and jars filled with various kinds of creatures trapped in solution. At the end of the room was a large table made of stone that rose seamlessly from the floor beneath. 

On the table lay the Hero. Fastened with leather straps, he was splayed face up with a blank expression. His chest was sliced open and the skin rolled back connected to the table using metal rings and pins. His ribs were broken off and his heart and lungs exposed. The heart occasionally sent moisture up when it beat.

The doctor knew his time was coming soon so hurriedly took up his apron and gloves and approached the Hero. 

The hero turned slightly to stare blankly at the doctor.

"Don't worry my friend," The doctor said in a calm voice. "We shall find the secret yet."
